output_contract.source: profiles.json.shared_worker_contract + active completion schema + result and human projections

v3.title: Cortex Worker Briefing v3 (artifact-backed semantic lifecycle)
v3.artifact_contract: The immutable briefing and native dispatch are authoritative. Workers publish semantic evidence and one conclusion through the action-specific tools; canonical results and human projections are server-derived outputs.
v3.failure_response_contract: Expected MCP validation or domain failure remains a tool-call error with a flat Cortex response. Use only public diagnostics and public recovery; never inspect Cortex source, cache, logs, ledger, session, environment, or hidden paths. Make only a deterministic same-operation correction explicitly authorized by that recovery. If a worker's first operation is pending trusted spawn observation, retry only that operation with bounded backoff until a finite deadline, without project access or replacement. Otherwise stop; incomplete public failure data fails closed.
v3.prompt_volume_guidance: Prompt volume targets are advisory worker guidance only. Prefer concise, complete evidence where practical, but never truncate, summarize away, reject, or omit material task, plan, result, event, question, answer, or artifact data to satisfy a byte, character, or file-size target. A complete payload may exceed any target and must be submitted intact; backend persistence stores the complete submitted content.

worker_completion_contract.worker_authority: Workers publish semantic conclusions only. Cortex derives lifecycle identity, provenance, workspace observations, and durable evidence.
worker_completion_contract.worker_bootstrap_observation: Resolve the first Cortex callable from ALL_TOOLS by its unique bare semantic name or host-namespaced suffix, then invoke the resolved callable exactly as its active public MCP declaration specifies, using the byte-for-byte server-issued authority wherever that declaration requires it. The active declaration is the sole source of call fields. ALL_TOOLS supplies name and description only; never require a local input schema or parameters object, and never assume a bare semantic name is directly callable. A worker's first operation can precede trusted observation of its native spawn. For that pending condition only, retry the same operation with bounded backoff until a finite deadline. A successful exact retry automatically clears the transient observer failure. Never access the project, switch operations, reconstruct authority, or spawn a replacement; at the deadline follow public fail-closed recovery.
worker_completion_contract.worker_question_pause: Only a genuine user decision classified by the active tool schema may become a durable user question. Internal technical conditions use server-owned recovery and never pause the user. After durably publishing one complete Unicode question, the worker ends its current native turn and is genuinely paused. It does not begin project work, poll, or submit until the real user answer is recorded and the same child resumes in a new native turn. Native child prose is never parsed as question authority.
worker_completion_contract.coordinator_waiting: After each native spawn_agent or followup_task, preserve the exact host-returned child identifiers and use wait_agent cycles with an explicit 300-second timeout for those exact bound children. No agents completed yet, timeout, an empty completion set, pendingInit, running, or any still-working child is nonterminal: immediately wait again for the same exact child identifiers and call no Cortex read or lifecycle tool. Terminal means only interrupted, completed, errored, shutdown, or notFound. Call read_worker_wave only after every exact bound child reports a terminal status; the backend independently verifies trusted terminal observation.
worker_completion_contract.briefing_terminal_authority: The worker briefing attributes exact terminal host authority to SubagentStop. Host MCP thread metadata is used only to bind the authorized worker call to its native child.
worker_completion_contract.coordinator_completion: Native V2 spawn_agent permits parallel wave members. The host binds the first authorized worker call to its exact native child within the root session. SubagentStop is the exact terminal host authority. Ordinary timeout-bounded waits are required progress control only; wait output is never completion evidence. A governance-close worker reads every supplied predecessor canonical result through the active predecessor-read tool and consumes every page before its dedicated closure submission; embedded projections do not create server read receipts. Once canonical results and matching terminal Stops are durable, read the current worker wave, follow the returned lifecycle direction, and deliver only after durable close evidence and required governance closure exist. This same-user local observation is not cryptographic proof or server attestation; unknown or unverifiable hook state fails closed.
worker_completion_contract.future_wave_adaptation: After reading a completed wave, make at most one evidence-frontier decision. Use revise_future_pipeline only for material changes to unexecuted future waves. Use append_rework_wave only when a completed canonical result itself needs product correction; it appends mutating rework plus independent verification without rewriting completed history. Technical failures use the server-owned exact-occurrence Luna-to-Terra-to-Sol replacement ladder with capability-safe profile resolution and never use either product operation. Exact replay is idempotent; stale or conflicting decisions are rejected. Dispatch every newly returned worker through native V2 spawn_agent, use ordinary generic waits, wait for matching terminal SubagentStop, read the canonical wave, then execute required governance closure before final handoff.

prompt_guidance_semantics: prompt_only_advisory; never a backend admission, storage, truncation, or rejection rule

source_ownership.worker_assignment_authorization: one exact opaque authority carried by the native dispatch
source_ownership.planner_shape: semantic work breakdown published through the current worker completion tool

prompt_eval.live_verification: development-only manual evidence in an ordinary interactive Codex CLI or tmux session; it is not a release gate or worker-lifecycle assertion
